findings.F1: Among bars where a coin closes above its Ichimoku cloud, the fewer days since it crossed above, the larger its next 5-day return above its normal drift. The slope on the log of days since crossing is -0.0215 (t -3.65, 490 non-overlapping cases), and the pattern holds in both halves of the windows (w1-w12: t -3.11, n 282; w13-w24: t -2.07, n 208).
findings.F2: By terciles of days above the cloud, the excess 5-day return is +3.53 % for 1 to 9 days (total move +4.11 %, about 21 times the 0.19 % cost of a round trip), +0.57 % for 9 to 19 days and -1.23 % for 19 to 39 days (163 to 164 cases each).
findings.F3: The freshness effect survives controls: with cloud width, distance above the cloud top and the 20-day return in the same regression, log days since crossing keeps beta -0.0222 (t -3.16, n 490), while width (t -0.15), distance (t 0.14) and the 20-day return (t 0.42) carry nothing; freshness and width are nearly uncorrelated (-0.08).
findings.F4: The freshness effect lasts beyond the tested horizon: over the next 10 days the slope on log days since crossing is -0.0350 (t -3.66, 432 cases on the 5-day grid, so the cases overlap).
findings.F5: The coins mostly agree on freshness: 5 of 6 coins have a negative slope (XRP t -2.86, LTC -1.70, ETH -1.63, ZEC -1.38, XMR -1.04), and BTC alone is flat (+0.0026, t 0.32, n 87).
findings.F6: The strategy's own record shows the same thing: active bars in their first 1 to 5 bars of the regime are followed by +2.76 % excess over 5 days (t 2.65, n 213), against -0.95 % to +0.29 % for later quartiles. The book, which holds through the whole stretch above the cloud, earns a mean daily return of 0.00046, just under the 0.0005 required.
findings.F7: The tested thinness gradient is carried by its tails, not by a steady slope: the lowest forecast quintile gives -1.78 % excess (t -2.11), the top quintile +2.48 % (t 2.14), and the middle three lie between +0.37 % and +0.59 % (about 170 cases each).
findings.F8: Two other patterns stood out but are not used for ideas:

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its Ichimoku cloud (9/26/52), its return over the next 5 days is larger the fewer days have passed since its close first rose above the cloud.
ideas.consequence: A trader would favour coins that have just broken above their cloud and give less weight to coins that have stood above it for weeks.
ideas.name: fresh cloud breakout continues

ideas.idea: When a coin closes above its Ichimoku cloud (9/26/52), its return over the next 10 days is larger the fewer days have passed since its close first rose above the cloud.
ideas.consequence: A trader could hold a fresh breakout above the cloud for about two weeks rather than one, since the extra rise keeps building past five days.
ideas.name: fresh breakout, ten-day rise
